nodes.label: HttpExtension
nodes.rationale: The HTTP module is built as an extension, deliberately separate from the I/O broker actors: HTTP servers do not fit the one-connection-many-messages shape, so they get their own DSL and backend abstraction rather than a BrokerActor subclass. system.http(port).bind(routes) is the shortcut over newServerAt/useBackend.

nodes.label: HttpServerBackend
nodes.rationale: The interface all three backends implement so the route DSL compiles identically and the backend only owns the listen/dispatch loop. Backend-specific ecosystems (Fastify schemas, Hono edge adapters, Express middleware) are not exposed through the DSL, and reaching for them drops cross-backend portability.

nodes.label: HttpClient
nodes.rationale: Wraps the runtime's native fetch, so it works identically on Bun, Node and Deno. Config layers as request > client > HOCON (actor-ts.http.client) > built-in defaults; a new HttpClient() built directly, with no system to read config from, keeps the built-in numbers.

nodes.label: HttpClient response bounds
nodes.rationale: A response is buffered in memory before the caller sees it, so the three things the remote peer controls are bounded by default: a 30 s deadline, an 8 MiB response ceiling, and 5 followed redirect hops. Past the ceiling the request is aborted while the body is still arriving and throws HttpResponseTooLargeError, so an oversized or endless response never finishes allocating.

nodes.label: Redirect hop policy
nodes.rationale: The client follows redirects itself rather than handing them to the platform, so decisions happen between hops: a cross-origin hop drops authorization, cookie and proxy-authorization so a redirect cannot walk a bearer token to a host you never chose; a 303 (and a 301/302 after POST) continues as GET with the body dropped so a write is never replayed against a second host; non-http(s) targets are refused; and the deadline and byte ceiling are cumulative over the chain. Refusals happen before the hop is issued, because a check on where a chain ended up has already made every request in it.

nodes.label: Out-of-domain bounds throw OptionsError
nodes.rationale: Every bound is enforced by a comparison and a NaN loses a comparison silently: a timeoutMs of NaN arms no timer, a maxResponseBytes of Infinity never trips, and neither raises anything - the bound just stops existing. So an out-of-domain value throws OptionsError before a socket is opened, checked when the call is made rather than only when the client is built. timeoutMs: 0 remains the one legitimate way to have no deadline.

nodes.label: One cache instance per middleware
nodes.rationale: InMemoryCache is LRU-bounded (10 000 entries by default) and its eviction is blind to what an entry protects. Share one instance and a caller who varies the response-cache key or the Idempotency-Key header evicts other clients' rate-limit counters and idempotency records, resetting their limits and re-running handlers on their retries.

nodes.label: HTTP handler as thin actor adapter
nodes.rationale: The common pattern: parse the request, ask an actor, marshal the reply. Business logic belongs in actors because route handlers run concurrently, so plain mutable state outside actors races like anywhere else in JavaScript, and a slow handler occupies a connection's lifetime until the server runs out of capacity.

hyperedges.label: Middlewares sharing an LRU cache evict each other's security state
